words.gloss: cow; release; daybreak (gosarga, lit. 'release of the cows'; standard)

hindi: जिसके मुख से गोसर्ग यानी प्रभात के समय पसीना बहुत अधिक टपकता है
english: He from whose face, at daybreak (gosarga), sweat drips profusely
notes: GROUPING: the sentence appears to continue in unit 84 ('tasya jīvitam' there). gosarga is literally 'release of the cows', the early-morning time; 'daybreak' is the standard sense. vadana = mouth or face; 'face' taken.

words.gloss: coating, smearing (lepa); fever (jvara); afflicted (upatapta, conjectural; printed upatana); lepa-jvara = a fever of the 'coating' kind, exact identity uncertain (disputed)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, लेपज्वर यानी लेप वाले ज्वर से पीड़ित का, जिस ज्वर की ठीक पहचान अनिश्चित है, उसका जीवन दुर्लभ है
english: On a conjectural reading, of one afflicted with lepa-jvara (a fever of the 'coating' kind, whose exact identity is uncertain), his life is hard to obtain

text_flags.why: possible: 'upatana' is not a known word; 'upatapta' (afflicted, heated) fits the sense and the ta/na and pta/ma OCR confusions seen in this print

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue unit 83 (daybreak sweat). The reading 'upataptasya' (afflicted) is conjectural and is adopted in both translations on that mark. 'lepa-jvara' perhaps corresponds to a fever with a coated, plastered feeling (Caraka's lepaka fever), but this is disputed and uncertain.

words.gloss: coral (pravāla); pellet, small ball (gulikā); appearing like (ābhāsa)
masūrikā: lentil-like eruptions (masūra = lentil); commonly taken as pox, smallpox-type (probable)

hindi: जिसके शरीर पर प्रवाल यानी मूँगे की गोलियों के समान दिखने वाली मसूरिकाएँ यानी मसूर के दाने जैसी फुंसियाँ, जो सम्भवतः चेचक जैसा रोग है
english: He on whose body there are masūrikā (lentil-like eruptions, probably a pox-type disease) that look like pellets of coral
notes: Spelling: printed 'prabāla' for 'pravāla' (v/b interchange in this print). Identification of masūrikā as smallpox or a pox-type eruption: probable (the name means 'lentil-like'). No verb in the unit; the sentence continues in 86.

hindi: उत्पन्न होकर शीघ्र नष्ट हो जाते हैं, वह देर से नहीं, थोड़े ही समय में नष्ट हो जाता है
english: Having arisen, (they) quickly vanish; before long (lit. not after a long time) he perishes
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 85. The plural subject of 'vinaśyanti' is not stated (probably the eruptions of 85); not supplied in the translation. 'na cirāt' = 'not after a long time', i.e. soon.

hindi: मसूर की फाड़ी के समान दिखने वाले तथा मूँगे के समान दिखने वाले
english: Resembling a split lentil, and likewise resembling coral
notes: Printed ḻ for l in 'vidaḻa' is the print habit (normalised to l). The nouns described are not in this unit; unit 88 gives 'visphoṭāḥ' (blisters), nominative plural, which the adjectives appear to qualify. Not supplied.

words.gloss: inside; mouth; having the mouth turned inward
kiṇa (scar, callus, hard mark; probable); appearing like

hindi: भीतर की ओर मुख वाले और किण के समान दिखने वाले, किण यानी सम्भवतः घट्टा या चोट का निशान, देह का नाश करने वाले विस्फोट यानी फफोले
english: Blisters (visphoṭa) with the mouth turned inward, looking like kiṇa (probably a scar or callus), destroying the body

text_flags.why: possible: visarga missing before the following k; the plural 'visphoṭāḥ' needs a plural adjective (a minor print slip; the sense is unchanged)

notes: 'kiṇa' is uncertain: scar, callus or weal; hedged. Printed 'visphoṭā' (visarga dropped before d) is regular sandhi. 'antarvaktra' = 'inward-mouthed' (the opening turned inward).

words.gloss: state of having shed flesh (loss of flesh)

hindi: दोनों आँखों में कामला यानी पीलिया, मुख भरा हुआ, और दोनों शंख यानी कनपटियों में माँस छूट जाने की अवस्था
english: Jaundice (kāmalā) in the two eyes, the face full, and in the two temples (śaṅkha) a state of shed flesh (loss of flesh)
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in 90 ('yasya taṃ parivarjayet'). The avagraha printed after -ā is a print habit (kāmalā + akṣṇoḥ). 'kāmalā akṣṇoḥ' could also be read as one compound; sense same. 'mukham pūrṇam' = face 'full' as printed (nothing added). śaṅkha = temple (standard).

hindi: जिसमें भय हो और शरीर में उष्णता हो, उसे त्याग देना चाहिए
english: He in whom there is fright (saṃtrāsa) and heat in the body, him one should avoid
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 89. The agent of 'parivarjayet' is not stated ('one'). 'aṅga' = body/limb; 'body' taken.

words.gram: pres. part. anu-√dhāv, n. nom. sg.

hindi: अचानक, पीछे दौड़ता हुआ, रगड़ा हुआ और त्वचा में आश्रित
english: Suddenly, running after (or along), and rubbed, resting in the skin
notes: Doubtful sense: 'anudhāvat' (running after) and 'vighṛṣṭa' (rubbed) are given literally without enrichment. The neuter singular forms do not agree with the plural 'vraṇāḥ' of unit 94, which the list in 91-94 appears to describe; the unit may be damaged or may qualify a different noun. Not resolved.

words.gloss: candana (sandalwood, Santalum album; standard); uśīra (root of vetiver, Chrysopogon zizanioides; standard); madirā (an intoxicating drink); kuṇapa (corpse); dhvāṅkṣa (crow); smelling of

hindi: चन्दन, उशीर यानी खस, मदिरा यानी नशीला पेय, कुणप यानी शव और ध्वाङ्क्ष यानी कौए की गन्ध वाले
english: Having the smell of sandalwood (candana), uśīra (vetiver root), madirā (an intoxicating drink), a corpse (kuṇapa) and a crow (dhvāṅkṣa)
notes: The noun described is not in this unit (the list 92-94 appears to describe the wounds, vraṇāḥ, of 94). 'kuṇapa-dhvāṅkṣa' taken as two separate smells (corpse, crow), not 'crow-corpse'. Identifications: candana = sandalwood, uśīra = vetiver root, both standard.

words.gloss: śaivāla (water-moss, an aquatic weed; precise plant disputed); kukkuṭa-śikhā (cock's comb); kuṅkuma (saffron, Crocus sativus; standard); āla (probably orpiment, yellow arsenic sulphide); maṣī (ink, soot); lustre (prabhā)

hindi: शैवाल यानी काई जैसी जल की वनस्पति, जिसकी ठीक पहचान विवादित है, मुर्गे की कलगी, कुंकुम यानी केसर, आल यानी सम्भवतः हरताल और स्याही की आभा वाले
english: Having the lustre of śaivāla (water-moss; the exact plant is disputed), a cock's comb, kuṅkuma (saffron), āla (probably orpiment) and ink
notes: 'kuṅkumāla' is read kuṅkuma + āla (orpiment, a yellow mineral; probable); kuṅkuma + ala is equally possible by sandhi. The 'lustre' is shared by the whole list; the noun described is not in the unit. śaivāla identity disputed.

hindi: भीतर दाह वाले, ऊष्मा से रहित, प्राणों का नाश करने वाले व्रण यानी घाव
english: Wounds (vraṇa) with inner burning, without heat, causing the destruction of life
notes: GROUPING: appears to end the list begun in 91-93. The adjectives 'antardāha' and 'nirūṣman' are given as printed: inner burning with no heat (nothing added about the outer part).

hindi: जो वात से उत्पन्न हो और पीड़ा के लिए न हो, और पित्त से उत्पन्न जो दाह के लिए न हो
english: The Vāta-born (one) which would not be for pain, and the Pitta-born (one) which would not be for burning
notes: GROUPING: continues in 96. The noun (probably vraṇa, see 94 and 98) is not stated; 'na' is carried to the second clause. Dative of purpose rendered 'for pain', 'for burning'. Vāta and Pitta are the doṣas; kept as names.
lines_deva: यो वातजो न शूलाय स्यान्नदाहाय पित्तजः
lines_iast: yo vātajo na śūlāya syānnadāhāya pittajaḥ

words.gloss: marma-born (marma: a vital spot, doctrinal term)

hindi: कफ से उत्पन्न जो पीब के लिए न हो, और मर्म यानी जीवन-स्थल से उत्पन्न जो पीड़ा के लिए न हो
english: The Kapha-born (one) which would not be for pus, and the marma-born (one; marma = vital spot) which would not be for pain
notes: GROUPING: continues 95; the finite verb and noun are carried from 95 and not supplied. 'marma-ja' = born at/of a marma (vital spot); no modern equivalent forced.
lines_deva: कफजो न च पूयाय मर्मजश्च रुजे न यः
lines_iast: kaphajo na ca pūyāya marmajaśca ruje na yaḥ

hindi: जहाँ चूर्ण से रहित होकर भी चूर्ण बिखरा हुआ-सा दिखने वाला और अचानक दिखाई देता है
english: Where one without powder, looking as if strewn with powder, and suddenly, is seen
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in 98 (form of śakti, dhvaja, etc.). The noun described (probably a wound) is not stated.

hindi: शक्ति यानी भाले, ध्वज यानी पताका आदि का रूप; उन सब व्रणों को त्याग देना चाहिए
english: The form of a spear (śakti), a banner (dhvaja) and so on; one should avoid all those wounds

text_flags.why: possible: anusvāra lost; sarvān + tān gives sarvāṃstān by regular sandhi

notes: 'śakti' taken as the weapon (spear); it could also mean 'power'. The verb of 'rūpam' is carried from 'dṛśyate' (97) and not supplied.

hindi: मल, मूत्र और वायु को वहन करने वाले तथा कृमियों वाले भगन्दर यानी गुदा के पास के नासूर को
english: Bhagandara (fistula in ano) that carries faeces, urine and wind, and has worms
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 98; 'bhagandaram' is the object of 'varjayet' there. 'vaha' = carrying/conveying; read as the fistula passing faeces, urine and wind through it.

words.gram: pres. part. caus. √pat, m. nom. sg.

hindi: घुटने से घुटने को टकराता हुआ, दोनों पैरों को उठाकर गिराता हुआ
english: Striking knee with knee, and, having raised the two feet, dropping (them)
notes: GROUPING: the relative clause continues in 101 ('yaḥ apāsyati ...').

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, जो बार-बार मुख को हटाता है, वह रोगी जीवित नहीं रहता
english: On a conjectural reading (vaktram), the patient who repeatedly turns his face aside does not live

text_flags.why: possible: 'vakra' (crooked) gives no sense with apāsyati; 'vaktra' (face) fits, with a dropped t (kt/k confusion)

notes: 'apāsyati' = apa + asyati ('throws aside'); 'turns aside' is the natural sense with 'face'. The reading 'vaktram' is conjectural.

hindi: दाँतों से नखों के अग्र भागों को काटता हुआ, और उन्हीं से केशों या तिनकों को
english: Cutting the tips of the nails with the teeth, and with those (teeth) hairs or blades of grass
notes: GROUPING: unit 101 already ends in a complete clause ('āturo na sa jīvati'), so 100-101 appears to be one sentence; 102-106 appears to be a second one, in which the participles of 102-103 appear to go with the 'yaḥ' clauses of 104-105 and the main clause of 106. The boundaries are not firm.

words.gram: pres. part. vi-√likh, m. nom. sg.
pres. part. √tāḍ (10th class), m. nom. sg.

hindi: भूमि को काष्ठ से कुरेदता हुआ, ढेले को ढेले से मारता हुआ
english: Scratching the ground with a piece of wood, striking a clod with a clod
notes: Continues the same series of actions (100-106).
lines_deva: भूमिं काष्ठेन विलिखन् लोष्टं लोष्टेन ताडयन्
lines_iast: bhūmiṃ kāṣṭhena vilikhan loṣṭaṃ loṣṭena tāḍayan

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, जिसके रोम खड़े हों, जिसका मूत्र गाढ़ा हो, जिसे सूखी खाँसी हो और ज्वर हो
english: On a conjectural reading (hṛṣṭaloma), he who has bristling hair, thick urine, dry cough and fever

text_flags.why: possible: 'dṛṣṭaloman' (hair seen) gives no sense; 'hṛṣṭaloman' (bristling hair) is the standard term and dṛ/hṛ is a likely OCR confusion

notes: GROUPING: the relative clause continues in 105-106. The reading 'hṛṣṭa' is conjectural and marked in the translations.
lines_deva: दृष्टलोमा सांद्रमूत्रः शुष्ककासी ज्वरी च यः
lines_iast: dṛṣṭalomā sāṃdramūtraḥ śuṣkakāsī jvarī ca yaḥ

hindi: जो बार-बार हँसता हुआ, बार-बार गुनगुनाता हुआ, पैर से शय्या पर आघात करता है
english: He who, repeatedly laughing, repeatedly humming (kṣveḍ), strikes the bed with his foot
notes: 'kṣveḍ' is a rare verb (to hum, murmur, or roar); 'humming' taken, sense not certain. GROUPING: the relative clause continues in 106.
lines_deva: मुहुर्हसन्मुहुः क्ष्वेडन् शय्यां पादेन हंति यः
lines_iast: muhurhasanmuhuḥ kṣveḍan śayyāṃ pādena haṃti yaḥ

words.gram: pres. part. vi-√mṛś, m. nom. sg.

hindi: बार-बार छिद्रों को छूता हुआ वह रोगी जीवित नहीं रहता
english: The patient who repeatedly touches the holes (chidra) does not live
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete the sentence begun at 102 (or 104). 'chidra' = holes or openings; which openings (e.g. of the body) is not stated. 'vimṛś' can also mean 'considering'; 'touching' taken. A reader may recheck.

words.gloss: upward; breath (breath drawn upward, laboured breathing; probable)

hindi: जिसकी श्वास ऊपर की ओर हो यानी सम्भवतः कष्टपूर्ण श्वास हो, जिसकी ऊष्मा चली गई हो, जिसके वंक्षण यानी जाँघों के जोड़ पीड़ा से पीड़ित हों, उसे
english: Him whose breath is upward (probably laboured breathing), whose heat has gone, whose groins (vaṅkṣaṇa) are afflicted by pain
notes: GROUPING: object of 'parivarjayet' in 108. 'ūrdhvaśvāsa' taken literally with the modern equivalent hedged. 'gata-ūṣman' = heat gone.

words.gram: pres. part. adhi-√gam, m. acc. sg.

hindi: और सुख न पाने वाले को बुद्धिमान त्याग दे
english: And him who does not obtain ease, the wise one should avoid
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 107.

hindi: जिसके विकार यानी विकृतियाँ बढ़ती हैं और प्रकृति यानी स्वाभाविक अवस्था क्षीण होती है
english: He in whom the abnormalities (vikāra) increase and the natural state (prakṛti) diminishes
notes: Doubled dd in 'varddhaṃte' is an orthographic habit (normalised to vardhante). GROUPING: continues in 110.

hindi: अचानक, अचानक उसके जीवन को मृत्यु हर लेती है
english: Suddenly, suddenly, Death takes away his life
notes: 'sahasā' is printed twice (emphatic repetition); kept as printed.

hindi: जिस रोगी को लक्ष्य करके वैद्य औषध को तैयार करने के लिए
english: Having in view whom as patient, a physician, to prepare medicine (auṣadha)
notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues in 112 ('yatamānaḥ na śaknoti'); the physician is the subject there.

words.gram: pres. part. ātm. √yat, m. nom. sg.

hindi: यत्न करता हुआ समर्थ नहीं होता; उसका जीवन दुर्लभ है
english: Striving, he is not able; his life is hard to obtain
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of 111.
lines_deva: यतमानो न शक्नोति दुर्लभं तस्य जीवितं
lines_iast: yatamāno na śaknoti durlabhaṃ tasya jīvitaṃ

words.gram: ppp. ava-√car caus., n. nom. sg.

hindi: जाना हुआ, बहुत बार सफल और विधि के अनुसार प्रयुक्त
english: Known, successful many times, and applied according to rule
notes: GROUPING: the noun (the medicine, auṣadham of 114) is not stated here. 'siddha' = accomplished (not the 'cooked' sense); 'avacārita' = administered (wording open).

hindi: जिसके लिए औषध सफल नहीं होता, उसका चिकित्सित यानी उपचार नहीं है
english: For whom medicine does not succeed, for him there is no treatment (cikitsita)
notes: GROUPING: 113 appears to describe the medicine ('known, accomplished many times, administered by rule') of which this unit speaks.
lines_deva: न सिद्ध्यत्यौषधं यस्य नास्ति तस्य चिकित्सितं
lines_iast: na siddhyatyauṣadhaṃ yasya nāsti tasya cikitsitaṃ

words.gram: pres. part. pass. √kḷp, n. loc. sg.

hindi: जिसके औषध या अन्न की तैयारी किए जाने पर विपर्यय यानी उलटा परिणाम हो
english: He for whom, when medicine or food is being prepared, there would be a reversal (viparyaya)
notes: 'viparyaya' = reversal or contrary result; it may be the reversal of the preparation or of its effect. 'kalpyamāne' taken with both nouns as a locative absolute. GROUPING: continues in 116.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, अचानक वर्ण यानी रंग आदि से स्वस्थ होने पर भी वह जीवित नहीं रहता
english: On a conjectural reading (varṇādeḥ): suddenly, from colour and the like, even one who is healthy does not live

text_flags.why: possible: 'varṇavādeḥ' cannot be construed ('vāda' speech, no -eḥ ending); 'varṇādeḥ' (colour and so on) fits and the extra 'va' may be an OCR repeat; also the words are printed without a space before 'svastho'

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 115 (a reversal in colour etc. as a sign). The sense is not firm: 'from colour and the like' is left as printed (nothing supplied). The reading is conjectural; a different emendation is possible.

hindi: वायुरहित स्थान में, ईंधन सहित भी जिसकी ज्योति बुझ जाती है
english: He whose light (jyotis), even with fuel, goes out in a windless place
notes: 'jyotis' = light or flame (a lamp or fire, not specified). 'ca api' is taken as 'even'. GROUPING: a separate sign from 116.

hindi: जिस रोगी के घर में फूटते हैं या गिरते हैं
english: Of the patient in whose house (ones) break or fall
notes: GROUPING: the subject 'amatrāṇi' (vessels) is in 119 and the sentence is completed there. 'yasya' agrees with 'āturasya' (of the patient). The translation keeps the stated words only.
lines_deva: आतुरस्य गृहे यस्य भिद्यंते वा पतंति च
lines_iast: āturasya gṛhe yasya bhidyaṃte vā pataṃti ca

hindi: अत्यधिक अमत्र यानी पात्र; उसका जीवन दुर्लभ है
english: Excessively, the vessels (amatra); his life is hard to obtain
notes: GROUPING: the verbs 'bhidyante vā patanti' of 118 are carried here. 'amatra' = a large vessel or pot (standard).

hindi: जिस दुर्बल मनुष्य को रोग अचानक छोड़ देता है
english: The weak man whom a disease suddenly leaves
notes: GROUPING: continues in 121. 'parimuñcati' = leaves, lets go; nothing added about recovery.
lines_deva: यं नरं सहसा रोगो दुर्बलं परिमुंचति
lines_iast: yaṃ naraṃ sahasā rogo durbalaṃ parimuṃcati

hindi: आत्रेय उसके जीवन को संशय को प्राप्त हुआ मानते हैं
english: Ātreya considers his life to have reached a state of doubt
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of 120. 'Ātreya' left as a name, no role added.

words.gloss: abnormal, altered (vikṛta); disease (vyādhi); to be understood (vijñānīya); name of the chapter

hindi: इस प्रकार विकृतव्याधिविज्ञानीय नामक ग्यारहवाँ अध्याय
english: Thus the eleventh chapter, named Vikṛtavyādhivijñānīya.
notes: Colophon. The chapter name is kept in Sanskrit; its parts mean roughly 'to be understood about abnormal (altered) diseases'. Hindi gives the name with hyphens as a name.
